text.p: Investors should not rule out the possibility of Morrison Petroleums Ltd mounting a reverse takeover bid doe much-smaller Canadian 88 Energy Corp, an analyst who follows both firms closely said on Monday.
"I can just speculate, but I wouldn't be too surprised if we see a bid for Canadian 88. It's called a 'Pac Man,'" ScotiaMcleod analyst Rob Robinson.
"This is speculation on my part, but I would put it in the context of if I were (Morrison chairman Gordon Stollery), I'd take a shot at Canadian 88."
Robinson said Morrison, target of a C$652-million bid announced by Canadian 88 on Monday, could view the suitor as a good acquisition for the same reasons Canadian 88 covets Morrison.
Both firms are large players in foothills deep gas exploration in southwest Alberta, where Morrison controls 123,000 net acres and Canadian 88 11,000, he said.

Morrison, following a series of asset sales and the creation of a royalty trust based on Alberta gas plant and British Columbia oil pipeline assets, has the financial wherewithall to complete such a deal, he said.
Still, Canadian 88's proposed cash and stock deal is viewed as a positive move for its shareholders, he said.

Morrison's stock has been depressed since December, when the company announced disappointing drilling results at its Racehorce Creek gas play, a result of investors taking a short-term view of the company's prospects, Robinson said.
Canadian 88 has been one of the Canadian energy industry's high-fliers since the company made a major natural gas discovery at nearby Waterton.

"The southern foothills belt in my view is one of the most prolific natural gas plays in North America," Robinson said. "The advantage to that play is it has infrastructure in place and it has plant capacity."
He said he estimated that the region harbors as much as 5.5 trillion cubic feet of natural gas.
